correctness.rationale: Normalizing by the lower diagonal unit gives B₂(R)≅R×₍units₎×(R⁺⋊R×₍units₎). At a fixed affine multiplier s, conjugation takes b to wb+(1−s)z, so translation classes are unit orbits on R/(1−s)R lifted through (1−s)R. If 1−s is a unit the quotient is trivial; if it is nonzero radical, its ideal is a k-line of size q; if s=1 the orbits are the units, the zero singleton and the nonzero radical lines. These give the six rows with coincident numerical sizes added. For the dual action, every radical character has q extensions; a nontrivial restriction is represented by a nonzero k-linear β via the trace pairing. Its stabilizer must reduce to 1, and invariance under 1+w is equivalent to β(w)=0 by testing χ(wr) over all residues r. It therefore has size q^{d−1}; the other orbits are the trivial character and the nontrivial quotient characters. Each invariant additive character extends to its inertia subgroup by being trivial on the stabilizer complement, so the abelian little-group rule gives the displayed degrees and multiplicities. These arguments apply to q=2, d=1, and mixed characteristic without a coefficient field. The class total, commuting probability and fixed-q limit follow by summation. Independent arithmetic (python3 /workspace/independent_arithmetic_checks.py) checked weighted class populations, degree squares and totals for 48 parameter pairs; the frozen checker was inspected, not executed.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The orbit descriptions work in even characteristic: the ideal of a nonzero radical element is a k-line, reduction gives all of k×, and each principal-unit translation of extensions is determined by the field character r↦χ(wr). For a nonzero radical character these exhaust the q characters of the residue additive group, by the nondegenerate trace pairing. Thus orbit sizes and stabilizer multiplicities do not use oddness. For each nonzero-radical multiplier lift quotient orbit sizes through the ideal of cardinality q, including q−1 per nonzero radical projective line; for residue not one use a single class of size |R| and for s=1 use the usual unit-multiplication orbits. The numbers of the three multiplier types are U−q^d, 1, and q^d−1. Multiplying by U for the central direct factor and adding coincident sizes gives all frozen rows. The total and limiting commuting law are direct summations. The odd prime restriction in the other finding is needed for its binomial group-power formula, not for this corroborating spectrum calculation.
